structure.title: Privilege at school
structure.text: Sara's arrival establishes the comforts money buys and her imaginative way of treating the people around her.

structure.title: Changed circumstances
structure.text: A reversal tests the school's kindness and Sara's understanding of dignity. Small acts matter within a large change of status.

people.text: A pupil with a rich imagination.

people.name: Becky

context.title: Money and treatment
context.text: Adults' apparent affection can depend on a child's social position. The school provides repeated comparisons of how rank shapes attention.
context.takeaway: Compare conduct before and after advantage changes.

context.title: Imagined royalty
context.text: Sara's princess ideal concerns conduct as much as wealth. Pretending becomes a way to preserve standards when others abandon theirs.
context.takeaway: Imagination can carry an ethical commitment.

notice.why: Kindness becomes measurable in material care.

notice.text: Notice whom Sara addresses as an equal.

opening: Sara Crewe arrives at boarding school with expensive clothes, a devoted father, and a headmistress eager to please. When the money disappears, the same adults discover reasons to treat her quite differently. Sara is sent upstairs to work and sleep in the cold, carrying an imagination that had once looked like another luxury. Burnett makes kindness matter in small, material ways: a shared meal, a word of recognition, the decision to regard someone as a person when the household has decided she is useful labour.
